**Pre-alpha.** The first public build of Hildegard: your own film studio, on your own GPU. Expect rough edges, and
please report them.

## Install

- **The app:** `Hildegard_x64-setup.exe` (Windows, no admin rights), `Hildegard_aarch64.dmg` (Mac with Apple
  silicon), `Hildegard_amd64.AppImage` or `.deb` (Linux). The app isn't signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and
  macOS Gatekeeper will ask you to confirm.
- **One line in a terminal:** `curl -fsSL https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.sh | sh` on macOS and Linux, or
  `irm https://dbaney.com/hildegard/install.ps1 | iex` in PowerShell. Then `hildegard setup`.
- Every file's SHA-256 is in `SHA256SUMS`, and the installers check each download against it.

## What works

- Direct shots with camera language (bodies, lenses, apertures, moves, looks) on LTX-2.5, LTX-2 and Wan 2.2, through
  ComfyUI, on NVIDIA, or AMD on Linux.
- The Choir: a Mac or laptop renders on another of your computers' GPUs over Tailscale.
- Host mode: your studio at an HTTPS link on your tailnet, with owners and directors.
- An MCP server, so Claude, Codex, Cursor and other AI apps can direct shots on your GPU.
- Hugging Face linking with the token kept in your OS keychain.
- The Omarchy bar widget.

## Known limits

- Macs don't render on their own GPU yet: on Apple's GPU the models come out blurred and take over an hour. Pair a
  Mac with a computer that has an NVIDIA or AMD GPU.
- LTX models follow Lightricks' license: free under $10M yearly revenue, and not for products that compete with
  Lightricks. Wan 2.2 is Apache-2.0.
